summary.headline: Tinna Rubber Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 31% to INR157 crores and PAT 45% to INR17 crores; H1 PAT up 60% to INR38 crores.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue reached INR157 crores (up from INR120 crores), with EBITDA of INR29 crores (18.8% margin) and PAT of INR17 crores (10.9% margin). H1 revenue rose 25% to INR313 crores, EBITDA 50% to INR63 crores (20.4% margin) and PAT 60% to INR38 crores (12.2% margin). Management said profitability moderated from Q1 due to start-up costs, geopolitical uncertainty and subsidiary performance, and reiterated FY27 guidance of about INR700 crores revenue, INR126 crores EBITDA and INR70 crores PAT. Expansion moved forward with a 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site (INR250 crores over 3 years), while the Saudi Arabia tyre recycling plant has been delayed by the West Asia conflict.

segments.name: Infrastructure
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 38% to INR112 crores despite bitumen supply constraints; management cites it as a main growth driver with Industrial, and notes monsoon and cold-weather seasonality in Q2 and Q4.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: H1 revenue grew 37% to INR85 crores; exports were about 6% of total revenue with export volume growth of about 15%.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: H1 revenue rose to INR21 crores from INR19 crores, driven by price correction with stable volumes.

segments.name: Steel (by-product)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose to INR57 crores from INR53 crores, mainly on price correction with stable volumes; management describes it as a by-product of tyre recycling.

segments.name: PCMB (Polymer Composites & Masterbatch)
segments.commentary: H1 revenue more than tripled to INR27 crores after 12,000 tpa added at Gannaur; capacity now 18,000 tpa, targeted at 8-10% of FY27 revenue and about INR70 crores top line. Management said this business runs at lower EBITDA margin than the core.

segments.name: TP Buildtech (associate)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR41 crores with EBITDA INR4.7 crores, contributing INR1 crore at consolidated level; best-case target of INR100 crores revenue by FY27.

segments.name: Oman subsidiary
segments.commentary: Ran at 90% utilisation in H1; EBITDA margin improved to 11.5% from 6.4% in FY26; PAT of INR1.3 crores in H1.

segments.name: South Africa and Saudi Arabia (start-up)
segments.commentary: Combined start-up loss of about INR94 lakhs in H1; South Africa Phase 1 complete with semi-processed exports begun, and 9,000 tpa crumb line delayed 3-4 months.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q2 EBITDA margin (about 16% per analyst) come off versus prior quarters, and what about PCMB mix and steel price trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said EBITDA margin was 18%-plus in Q2 (reported 18.8%), Q1 was an aberration with raw material and inventory benefits, and PCMB runs at lower margin than core as a new business still stabilising with R&D spend.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company's sourcing and margin stability differentiated versus peers hit by geopolitics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited diversity of geography, raw material base and customer base, pan-India presence, and multiple tyre origins, without commenting on competitors.

qa_highlights.question: Where is India capacity being added to reach 235,000 tpa, and by when?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10-15k tpa comes from debottlenecking, South Africa adds about 10k tpa this year, and Saudi (24k tpa) is delayed; the 40-acre Andhra Pradesh site is needed as existing land is largely exhausted.

qa_highlights.question: How will the INR250 crores Andhra Pradesh capex be funded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said funding options are open over the next 6 to 12 months given a strong balance sheet; the INR250 crores is exclusively Tinna Rubber and spread over 3 years.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the Saudi plant and the Panipat land acquisition risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Saudi land is allotted and contractors identified, but no advances released pending local stabilisation; Panipat is a fully depreciated plant of under 2 acres that could be moved within 3-4 months, and management is making representations to the state government.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue potential from Andhra Pradesh and what is Vision 2029 INR1,000 crores implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capex to sales of 2.5-3x implies INR250-300 crores revenue from INR100 crores capex; INR1,000 crores by FY29 is reachable with Andhra and Saudi, with 5-10% variance possible.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee and other expenses rise this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited front-ended hiring ahead of projects (growth of 20-30% annually), start-up costs, and provision for performance bonus in Q2.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue target of about INR700 crores reiterated; management said it is roughly halfway there at H1 (INR313 crores).
FY27 EBITDA target of INR126 crores and PAT of INR70 crores reiterated; management aims for EBITDA margin of 18% plus and at least 10% PAT conversion.
PCMB to contribute 8-10% of FY27 revenue, about INR70 crores top line this year, and at least INR125 crores next year.
Tyre pyrolysis and rCB business expected to earn EBITDA margin around 18%, similar to core; rCB production starts Q3 with commercial sales from Q4.

Vision 2029 targets: INR1,000 crores revenue, revenue CAGR above 25%, profitability CAGR above 33%, EBITDA margin above 18%, ROCE above 30%, and expansion from 8 to 10 locations. Management said INR1,000 crores by FY29 is within reach, with 5-10% variance possible.

Saudi Arabia plant construction expected to begin in H2 FY27, subject to geopolitical situation; no advances or payments released yet. Oman: no further capex planned; Saudi to take about INR25 crores more.
capex_capacity: Completed INR45 crores of capex in H1 out of INR100 crores planned across FY27 and FY28.
3,500 tpa micronised rubber powder expansion on track for Q3 FY27 commissioning, taking MRP capacity to 20,000 tpa.
PCMB capacity added 12,000 tpa at Gannaur, now 18,000 tpa; PCMB capacity 32,500 tpa was referenced by an analyst as a future target.

Acquired 40 acres in Andhra Pradesh for integrated tyre, plastics recycling, pyrolysis and rCB complex; about INR250 crores over 3 years, with about INR100 crores expected in FY27-FY28; groundbreaking expected as early as November. Capex to sales about 2.5-3x. INR250 crores is exclusively Tinna Rubber.

Installed India tyre-crushing capacity about 185,000 tpa plus Oman 15,000 tpa (total about 200,000 tpa); FY27 guidance of about 235,000 tpa India capacity was questioned, with management citing debottlenecking of 10-15k tpa, South Africa about 10,000 tpa this year, and Saudi 24,000 tpa delayed. Utilisation 85-90%. South Africa 9,000 tpa crumb line delayed 3-4 months. Current pyrolysis and downstream capacity 100 tonnes per day. Renewables met 40% of power needs in H1, capacity up from 1.23 MW to 4.48 MW.
demand_pricing: H1 tyre crushing volumes up 30% YoY to 86,000 tonnes; MRP, reclaimed rubber production up 19%; steady tyre-industry demand.
Infrastructure revenue up 38% to INR112 crores in H1 despite bitumen supply constraints; Industrial up 37% to INR85 crores with exports about 6% of revenue and export volume up about 15%.
Consumer and Steel revenue up on price correction with stable volumes; Steel revenue INR57 crores from INR53 crores.

Management said customers accepted price increases taken in recent months; recycled rubber more compelling as natural and synthetic rubber prices rose; company operates at optimal utilisation with low inventory.
Analyst noted H1 revenue per tonne (ex-PCMB) fell about 8%; management attributed it to product mix change, not price. rCB priced at least 30-35% below virgin carbon black.
risks_watch: Start-up losses and delays: South Africa crumb line delayed 3-4 months; Saudi Arabia 24,000 tpa plant on hold due to West Asia conflict; equipment stuck in Middle East.
Input cost and logistics volatility: freight and energy costs higher and more erratic over the last 4-5 months; mix of domestic and imported tyres; pyrolysis feedstock imports not permitted.
Capacity gap versus 235,000 tpa India target; FY27 capacity additions depend on debottlenecking and South Africa.
Panipat plant land possible acquisition by Haryana government; company representation pending.
PCMB and pyrolysis/rCB still ramping, with lower margin for PCMB; rCB sales Q4 onward; pyrolysis oil revenue for Q2 not disclosed.
EPR income fell to about INR4.6 crores in Q2 from INR6.7 crores in Q1; monitor next quarter.
Funding of Andhra Pradesh and Saudi capex not yet decided; management to decide over 6-12 months.
key_quotes: We have completed INR45 crores of capex in H1 out of INR100 crores planned across FY27 and FY28.
But the guidance we have given, and I'm pleased to say that we have met those targets is that our business model shows our ability to deliver 18% plus, and we are delivering that.
So all combined to get to INR1,000 crores by FY29 is very much in our reach.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the top-line and margin targets and on the balance sheet, but evasive on specifics: declined to share procurement costs, pyrolysis oil Q2 revenue, Chile investment size and India capacity breakup, promising follow-up later. Caution is shown on Saudi timing and geopolitics.
